theme: FX and purchasing power: exchange-rate history (ECB, BIS, FRED), broad-dollar indices, PPP/Big Mac, tourist affordability indices, company FX-exposure tooling
queries_run: site:github.com ECB exchange rate historical dataset csv
big mac index github data csv
FRED exchange rates python client github
BIS effective exchange rate index github dataset

candidates.name: TheEconomist/big-mac-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Economist Big Mac Index source repo: big-mac-raw-index.csv, big-mac-adjusted-index.csv (GDP-adjusted), big-mac-full-index.csv. Fields: local currency price, exchange rate, dollar price, index vs USD/EUR/GBP/JPY/CNY, GDP per capita, GDP-adjusted valuation. Multi-country, semi-annual since 2000, updated through 2022+ methodology change (McDonald's-provided US pricing from Jul 2022). Includes calculation notebook/R scripts.
candidates.why_useful: Direct PPP/affordability cross-country series -- a standard proxy for real currency over/undervaluation that could feed a cross-border demand/affordability adjustment for ABNB's international nights and ADR mix (gap area: PPP/Big Mac in theme, tangential to gap 6/7 consumer strength by country).
candidates.last_activity: recent (64 commits, ongoing per README methodology notes through 2022+)

candidates.name: datasets/exchange-rates
candidates.what_it_holds: Frictionless-Data/Open Knowledge Foundation packaged FX dataset sourced from FRED (fred.stlouisfed.org). Daily, monthly and yearly CSVs with Date, Country, Value fields (USD/currency or currency/USD by country convention). Datapackage.json schema included; automated maintenance workflow.
candidates.why_useful: Ready-to-use multi-country FX time series in tidy CSV form, no API key needed -- can substitute/cross-check our current FRED FX pull (~40 series) with a pre-packaged, versioned alternative and is trivially reproducible.
candidates.last_activity: 55 commits, automated update workflow present (exact date not shown)
candidates.time_coverage: Historical through FRED's series length (varies by currency, several decades for majors)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps with our existing FRED FX schedules holding; flagged because it is a pre-cleaned, versioned CSV mirror rather than a raw API pull

candidates.name: mortada/fredapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Python wrapper for FRED AND ALFRED (Archival FRED) web services. Returns pandas Series/DataFrames. Supports get_series_first_release, get_series_as_of_date, get_series_all_releases, get_series_vintage_dates -- i.e., true point-in-time/vintage retrieval of any FRED series including FX and broad-dollar indices (e.g. DTWEXBGS).
candidates.why_useful: Directly serves the point-in-time/vintage rule (repo rule #2) and gap 4 (ALFRED-style macro vintages) -- lets us pull the broad trade-weighted dollar index or any FX series exactly as it was known on a given guide date, rather than the revised/current value.
candidates.last_activity: 67 commits; examples reference data through Oct 2024
candidates.geography: US Fed / global series available via FRED
candidates.time_coverage: Whatever the underlying FRED/ALFRED series covers (broad dollar index back to 2006 for DTWEXBGS, older majors longer)
candidates.size_hint: small python library, no data committed (pull-on-demand)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already use FRED for ~40 series but likely not via ALFRED vintages -- this closes that point-in-time gap

candidates.name: fawazahmed0/exchange-api (successor to currency-api)
candidates.what_it_holds: Git-based, daily-updated JSON currency exchange rate files (200+ currencies, plus crypto/metals) served via jsDelivr/Cloudflare CDN, but the underlying data is committed to the git history day by day -- so cloning history gives a de facto daily point-in-time FX panel back to when the project started (repo shows queries working from at least 2024-03-06 forward; older history may exist in git log). Prettified and minified JSON per date.
candidates.why_useful: Because each day's rates are a separate git-tracked JSON snapshot, this is one of the few free FX sources that is inherently point-in-time/vintage-correct (rule #2) rather than a rewritten current-value table -- useful for reconstructing what a spot rate looked like on any specific historical date without paying for a vendor terminal.
candidates.last_activity: 111 commits, active GitHub Actions daily publish workflow
candidates.time_coverage: Daily, from project start (~2023) to present
candidates.size_hint: many small JSON files, cumulative history could be sizeable via git log
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: New angle vs our existing FX schedules: vintage-correctness via git history

candidates.name: expersso/BIS
candidates.what_it_holds: R package with get_datasets() and get_bis() functions that download and parse BIS (Bank for International Settlements) CSV datasets into a unified format: policy rates, exchange rates, nominal and real effective exchange rate (EER) indices, credit statistics, property prices, at daily/monthly/quarterly/annual frequencies.
candidates.why_useful: Gives a one-command pull of BIS broad effective exchange rate indices (a standard 'broad-dollar-index' analogue for other currencies, e.g. EUR EER, JPY EER) that we do not currently hold -- useful for constructing a multi-currency trade-weighted FX basket beyond just USD, relevant to ABNB's EMEA/APAC/LatAm revenue mix.
candidates.license: not explicitly shown on page (unofficial/community R package, unaffiliated with BIS)
candidates.last_activity: 6 commits (low activity, but BIS's own data endpoints are stable)
candidates.time_coverage: BIS EER series generally 1994-present per BIS's own archive
candidates.size_hint: small R package, data pulled live from BIS servers (not committed)

candidates.name: tgherzog/wbgapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Python module for the World Bank's API -- pythonic querying of any World Bank Open Data indicator series (economies x series x time) including PA.NUS.PPP (PPP conversion factor, LCU per international $), PA.NUS.FCRF (official exchange rate), and related affordability/consumer-price indicators, across all World Bank member countries.
candidates.why_useful: One-command pull of World Bank PPP conversion factors and official FX rates by country/year -- a broader and longer-run complement to the Big Mac index for tourist-affordability comparisons across ABNB's LatAm/APAC markets (gap 7 regional travel volume context).
candidates.last_activity: 142 commits; README examples reference 2020-2021 data (module itself pulls live, current data)
candidates.size_hint: small python library, no data committed (pull-on-demand)

candidates.name: OpenBB-finance/OpenBB
candidates.what_it_holds: Large open-source 'investment research platform' (73k+ stars, 6800+ commits) aggregating many data providers behind one Python/CLI interface, including forex/FX modules pulling from multiple upstream providers (some free, many require third-party API keys). No committed dataset -- it is integration plumbing.
candidates.why_useful: Could be used as a single client to assemble ad hoc FX, macro and equity data pulls (including peer 8-K-style data and options) without hand-rolling each API wrapper, but most useful feeds need a paid key so value is mainly as a convenience layer, not a new data source.
candidates.last_activity: very active (6863 commits on develop, current)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps broadly with things we already source directly (FRED, options chains); flagged low because of key requirements

candidates.name: RomelTorres/alpha_vantage
candidates.what_it_holds: Python wrapper for the Alpha Vantage API's FX endpoints (get_currency_exchange_rate and related forex time-series calls), returning pandas DataFrames. Requires a free Alpha Vantage API key (not a paid key, generous free tier).
candidates.why_useful: Cheap way to pull historical daily FX time series for currency pairs relevant to ABNB's regional mix (EUR, GBP, MXN, BRL, AUD, JPY vs USD) if FRED coverage of a specific cross is thin; also has stock/equity time series in the same client.
candidates.last_activity: not shown but actively maintained, widely used package
candidates.time_coverage: Whatever Alpha Vantage's free tier exposes (typically full daily history for majors)
candidates.size_hint: small python library, no data committed
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps with our existing FX schedules; only useful if a specific cross is missing

candidates.name: owid/owid-datasets (Our World in Data, archived)
candidates.what_it_holds: Archived (as of 14 Apr 2025) OWID collection of CSV+datapackage social/economic indicator datasets by country; likely includes historical PPP and exchange-rate-adjusted GDP series (could not confirm exact folder contents from the fetched page -- OWID's live Grapher/ETL and Chart API at ourworldindata.org now supersede this repo for current data). Worth a follow-up directory listing if pursued.
candidates.why_useful: If it still contains PPP/exchange-rate-adjusted series in committed CSV form, it would be a long-run, easy-to-diff complement to the Big Mac index and World Bank PPP factors for tourist affordability comparisons.
candidates.license: unspecified in fetched content (OWID data typically CC BY)
candidates.time_coverage: unclear from fetch, likely multi-decade per OWID convention

No dedicated 'company FX-exposure regression tool' repo was verified this pass -- that sub-area of the theme remains uncovered and is worth a targeted follow-up (search terms: 'currency exposure elasticity regression github', 'FX translation hedge model python github', 'natural hedge FX 10-K analysis tool github').
